task: Lattice CLI needs explicit Conservative, Authority-Verified, and Full Autopilot execution modes for unattended host-to-host development while preserving policy, evidence, receipt, review, and merge authority boundaries.
outcome: User runs `lattice autopilot_run --mode=conservative --storyId=B-demo --policy=fake --json` and sees a structured result saying mode=conservative, status=manual_review_ready, validation=passed, mergePlan.manualOnly=true, productionDone=false; docs also show authority-verified and full-autopilot boundaries.
facts: B-8a1a already delivered policy-bound dispatch_auto with Claude Code real subprocess support under allowRealHostSubprocess=true and claude --print <prompt-file> command allowlist.
Current dispatch_review and dispatch_merge_plan intentionally keep authorityChanged=false, receiptVerified=false, productionDone=false, and manualOnly=true for local diagnostic results.

Codex, Claude Code, and Gemini can call each other as CLIs, so Lattice should primarily provide policy, handoff, evidence, receipts, review, and merge boundaries rather than replacing host intelligence.
Conservative mode must be the safe default: automatic development evidence is allowed, automatic production authority is not.
Authority-Verified and Full Autopilot modes are high-risk because they touch completion semantics, story lifecycle, and production/main merge wording.
constraints: Do not weaken existing dispatch_auto policy checks, allowedPaths/deniedPaths, commandAllowlist, env filtering, or Claude Code only real subprocess boundary.
Do not allow any local diagnostic receipt to satisfy server authority receipt requirements.
Do not auto-merge main or claim productionDone unless an explicit mode policy and required authority gates pass.
All long-running loops must be bounded by maxIterations, maxRuntimeMinutes, maxBudgetUSD, stopOnConflict, and stopOnScopeViolation.
Reuse existing dispatch, receipt, validation, and merge_plan primitives instead of introducing a second runner stack.
unknowns: Whether authority server receipt verification can be fully live-tested in this story or should be represented by an explicit fake-authority deterministic smoke.
How much story-branch integration can safely be automated without fighting existing DONE merge worktree gates.
Whether host-native delegation should be a first-class run mode in this story or a documented contract surfaced through autopilot plan output.
How much auto-fix behavior should be implemented now versus limited to bounded retry/state classification.
